{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZgsv5g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDHw2Q", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 57, "title": "Correct WD2793 Type-II settling and rotational sector searches", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `0c80c26c18b03f57e5ab9744a409ae9339615e28`, `crates/msx-core/src/disk.rs:367–381` ignores the Type-II E flag and immediately rejects side-compare mismatches. `start_sector()` at lines 489–510 immediately accepts valid geometry or rejects mismatched tracks, absent sides and invalid sectors. Multi-record continuation repeats this shortcut.

For example, requesting sector 10 on ready media immediately reports record-not-found. Successful requests expose DRQ after only 114 CPU cycles regardless of rotational position. These discrepancies affect ordinary firmware polling and disk-loader timing; no specific commercial-game failure is established.

## Expected outcome

Both Weave and Philips interfaces use distinct Type-II settling, rotational search and transfer phases. Read/write requests find matching synthetic IDs before entering the existing byte-transfer model. Unmatched requests remain BUSY until the search limit. Preserve completed Type-I work and existing media safeguards.

## Context

Local HEAD matches GitHub main. Open Issue/PR inspection returned none. [Issue #53](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/53) and [PR #54](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/54) implemented Type-I verification and explicitly deferred sector-transfer timing.

Inspected technical evidence:

- [TI TMS279X/WD279X manufacturer transcription](https://deramp.com/swtpc.com/DC_5/TMS279X_DataSheet.pdf), printed pages 10, 12–13, 17 and 20: E-controlled settling, cylinder/sector/optional-side comparison, index-limited failure and ascending multi-record searches. Apply the 1 MHz WD2793 profile: 30 ms settling. This edited second-source document is not physical WD2793 measurement; earlier WD scan/handbook access failures remain limitations.
- [Pinned openMSX WD2793](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/WD2793.cc), `startType2Cmd`, `type2Loaded`, `type2Search` and `type2Rotated`: corroborates scheduled settling/search. Optional head comparison remains TODO and stopped-rotation handling is explicitly uncertain.

`docs/disks.md:240–284` already defines synthetic IDs, rotation, rounding and Type-I boundary ordering. Raw DSK supplies payloads, not measured track layout. Reuse that documented approximation.

Native disk/Philips/Type-I and browser fixtures are present. [Inspected CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/40037811888/job/120701477035) report 223 Rust and 122 browser passes on a tree matching main. Existing assertions include immediate RNF and therefore do not validate this correction. Planning ran no builds or tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement E=1 settling before search for ready, writable Type-II requests; E=0 skips this delay. Retain the HLT-high assumption. Keep fractional deadlines: 30 ms equals 107386.35 CPU cycles. BUSY remains set and DRQ/IRQ inactive during settling/search.
- [ ] Encounter IDs using the existing 300 rpm, nine-sector profile. Match Track against the physical-cylinder ID and Sector against its sector number; C=0 ignores S, while C=1 compares S with the ID-side LSB. Missing sides supply index without IDs. Payload contents must not fabricate CRC or address-mark errors.
- [ ] Unmatched searches fail on the fifth observed rising index. Reuse and document existing search-start inclusion and ID-before-index ordering as selected model policies, without claiming silicon confirmation. Preserve immediate not-ready rejection at command acceptance. Retain existing Type-II control-change cancellation, extending it through settling/search; document that policy separately from physical behavior.
- [ ] Define the bounded synthetic handoff explicitly: after a matching ID, retain the existing 114-cycle first-DRQ delay, service-relative subsequent bytes and service timeout. These remain approximations. Consume only residual elapsed time after each phase transition; large, irregular and single-cycle ticks must agree through first DRQ and pending-byte timeout. Do not begin transfer before the matching event.
- [ ] Multi-record completion increments Sector and starts a fresh rotational search without repeating E settling or crossing tracks automatically. After sector 9, sector 10 remains BUSY until its search fails. Preserve completed sector writes; cancellation must never commit an incomplete staged sector.
- [ ] FORCE INTERRUPT, reset, mount/eject and interface removal cancel pending phases without later resurrection. Preserve write protection, exact export, dirty-media guards, private ownership, interface decoding and IRQ/DRQ polarity/acknowledgement.
- [ ] Add independently calculated timestamp/status/data regressions for read/write, E values, all nine ID positions, revolution wrap, cylinder/sector/side mismatches, C/S combinations, both geometries, fifth-index boundaries, multi-record continuation and cancellation in every new phase. Check immediately before/at/after deadlines. Replace obsolete immediate-success/RNF assumptions across disk, Type-I and Philips tests. Record meaningful baseline failures and corrected results.
- [ ] Extend original CPU-executed Philips diagnostics on both models to poll delayed success/failure, read known payloads and export exact writes. Exercise compiled Wasm at `/` and `/msx-rust/`. Adjust fixture polling budgets from documented emulated bounds. Preserve MSX1/MSX2 video/input, PSG/SCC/SCC-I audio, firmware/sub-ROM/mapper coexistence, SRAM and provenance behavior. No BIOS bypasses or proprietary prerequisites.
- [ ] Update affected disk documentation and validation records. Keep byte-cadence/lost-data correction, physical spin-up, full HLD lifecycle, protected formats and additional commands separate. The Coordinator runs and reports `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`, using README setup. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings before merge; distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Before merge, compare original register traces with the pinned upstream configuration, accounting for its unresolved side/no-rotation behavior. Additional checks may use software already lawfully available. These comparisons were not performed during planning; diagnostic success does not establish commercial playability.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
